g.text: Generalised. Farming areas, crop fields, farms and irrigation:
Atlas of Namibia 2022 data (CC BY 4.0). Regions: NSA (CC BY
3.0 IGO). Towns: GeoNames. East–west scale within 5%.
Dryland crops and dense crop fields lie across the north, densest
in the north-central regions, with more along the northern border
Inside the commercial farms, central areas are mainly cattle;
farther south (Hardap, //Karas) sheep and goats dominate, with
Irrigation areas, e.g. near Mariental and on the southern border
(the Orange River), are local crop sites inside livestock areas:
The largest block of crop-field cells covers Oshana, eastern
Omusati, western Ohangwena and north-western Oshikoto: a
north-central cluster by the Angolan border.
Farther east, crop fields form narrower patches along the
northern border near Rundu and in Zambezi.
Fields thin out westwards across Omusati and are almost absent in
Kunene. The cells show where fields are dense (mostly household
farms), not the purpose of every field.
One small plot is keyed vegetables for sale: a small-scale
It lies next to the town and beside the road, close to buyers and
The other plots are keyed only as cultivated, so the inset does
not show whether they are sold or used at home: it shows one sale
Commercial farms cover most of central and southern Namibia;
their northern edge runs south of Etosha and the northern
They produce different livestock: mainly cattle in central areas
(Otjozondjupa, Omaheke, Khomas) but mainly sheep and goats in
The hatched Otavi–Grootfontein–Tsumeb triangle is a crop area far
inland, inside the central cattle zone and not near the coast.
